Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

defeat noun and verb

also defeated, be defeated, conquer, lose a battle, suffer a defeat

classical

Sall. Jug. 59.3 (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 22.51.11: clādem accipere (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 186
Traupman 302

clādēs, clādis f.

noun, third declension

a defeat, a disaster

Any disaster, and in war a defeat (Lewis & Short). To suffer a defeat, clādem accipere (Traupman 186).

Other words

  • vincō, vincere, vīcī, victum — defeat, beat (an enemy, a rival)

    verb, third conjugation · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.42; Traupman 186; Traupman 295; Traupman 302

    To be defeated, vincī; the defeated, victī.

  • superō, superāre, superāvī, superātum — overcome, defeat

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.40 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 186

  • repulsa, repulsae f. — a defeat at the polls, rejection of a candidate

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “a refusal, denial, repulse in soliciting for an office”; Traupman 302

Examples

  • sī vīcērunt, efferunt sē laetitiā, victī dēbilitantur animōsque dēmittunt

    if they win, they are carried away with joy; if they are beaten, they lose their strength and their spirits sinkCic. Fin. 5.42

  • Vae victīs.

    Woe to the beaten!Plaut. Ps. 1317

  • comitiīs repulsa

    a defeat at the pollsTraupman 302

  • repulsa cōnsulātūs

    defeat in running for the consulshipTraupman 302

  • repulsam ferre

    to suffer a defeat (in an election)Traupman 302

  • clādem accipere

    to suffer a defeat (in battle)Traupman 302

See also victory, win, lose, battle, war.
